x: This was won by Jim Morris, a very fine walker, but it seemed as if Harry Churcher was a little tired, which is not to be wondered at in view of his very strenuous season on the track.

In the Southern Counties 2 miles Championship at Uxbridge, four of our walkers competed and once again Harry led the field to win in the excellent time of 13.53, eleven seconds in front of Jim Morris and beating Bert Cooper's 1935 time of 13.54.
Our Cadogan members in the Middlesex Championship did not fare so well, with the exception of Bob Readman who finished second to Jim Morris, the team being fourth.

This race produced the largest field so far of the season and of the 205 starters, Harry Churcher soon went to the front and walked a very fast race to finish well ahead of Jim Morris who was making one of his rare appearances.
He followed this up on February 22nd by winning the Police 10 miles championship in the second fastest time ever recorded, 80 mins. 11 secs., only 52 secs. outside Jim Morris's record.

Hugh Mc Greechan was almost back to his very best form, George Beecham turned in his usual reliable Championship performance, Jim Morris did splendidly on his first effort, and George Checkley whipped in a really excellent team of eight men.
